summary: Add a library figure showing how lowest-locant numbering decides a branched name, plus MCQs with misconception distractors for the two outcomes (hydrocarbon/alkane definitions) that currently have only recall-style short items.

improvements.caption: Numbering a branched chain both ways to find the lowest locant for the methyl substituent
improvements.where: note, after the Method's naming step (step 3)
improvements.why: Shows, side by side, numbering from each end of 3-methylhexane and why only the lower locant (3, not 4) is used; the diagram table has no type for this and the note currently only states the rule in words.

Both outcomes have six short recall items each but no MCQ and no item with a distractor tied to misconception m1 (treating C–H bonds as a functional group); the only MCQs in the pack are on formulas and naming (13.1.3-13.1.6).
improvements.what: Two generated MCQs: one asking which of a hydrocarbon/non-hydrocarbon pair is NOT a hydrocarbon and why; one asking whether an alkane has a functional group, with a distractor keyed to m1 ('it has a functional group because of its C–H bonds').

improvements.why: This outcome also has only short recall items; no item carries a distractor tied to misconception m2 (same molecular formula implies same properties), even though m2 is defined in the pack.
improvements.what: One generated MCQ giving two isomers/compounds with the same molecular formula but different functional groups, asking which has a stated characteristic property, with a distractor keyed to m2.
